name: Corn Dolly

attributes.attribute: built from the last sheaf at harvest

sources: Meaden, George Terrence. The Goddess of the Stones: The Language of the Megaliths. London: Souvenir Press, 1991, 204-205.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Corn Dolly, otherwise the Corn Maiden, is a folkloric image shared by Scotland and Ireland. At harvest folk wove straw into a roughly human shape, often taking the final sheaf for the work. Its dim past is plainly mythic or ritual. The Dolly relates to two figures of debated years, the hag the Cailleach and the Bride Brigit, the second perhaps the hag's maiden aspect. From fall to spring it rested in a home or barn, figuring in sowing and the like as rites of new life.

okr.objective: The Corn Dolly is a harvest symbol of folklore.
key_results: It was shaped from straw at harvest.
It used the last sheaf of the field.
It links the Cailleach and the Bride.
It was kept from autumn to spring.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
